currentContext.expansion: Oil and Gas: to maximise recovery from the KG D6 field, four infill wells are planned targeting incremental ~220 BCF of gas, with three additional workover wells planned in FY2026-27 for production sustenance. Exploration surveys (including Controlled Source Electromagnetic Survey) are underway in blocks KG-UDWHP-2018/1, KG-UDWHP-2022/1 and GS-OSHP-2022/1, which have received Petroleum Exploration Licenses under OALP Rounds II, VIII and IX; Infrastructure-led Exploration (ILX) prospects have matured into drilling plans in KG D6. In Coal Bed Methane, a multi-lateral horizontal well (MLW) programme (first of its kind in India) is being implemented in block SP(West)-CBM-2001/1 to reverse field decline — the first campaign is complete and the second is underway; Reliance Gas Pipeline Limited (a subsidiary) operates the 304-km Shahdol-Phulpur pipeline connecting CBM fields to the National Gas Grid. New Energy: the Dhirubhai Ambani Green Energy Giga Complex in Jamnagar is being developed across 5,000 acres with 44 million sq. ft. of manufacturing/operational built-up area, envisioned as the world's most integrated clean-energy manufacturing ecosystem outside China and expected to create over 200,000 green jobs. In Solar PV, core manufacturing assets were commissioned and Phase I became operational in FY2025-26, with cell and module lines being progressively commissioned and HJT cell production ramping up (first 200 MWp of HJT modules delivered); the facility remains on track to scale to 10 GWp per annum with expansion to 20 GWp planned, targeting 26% module efficiency, with polysilicon, glass, ingots and wafers being commissioned in phases toward full integration. The BESS giga-factory is in advanced commissioning, with civil construction complete and equipment installation underway; production will ramp through the second half of 2026, focused on LFP chemistry for utility-scale BESS and mobility, with 40 GWh of annual capacity to be operationalised and a roadmap to 100 GWh. In Green Hydrogen, RIL secured exclusive technology licensing from Nel ASA for alkaline electrolysers in India (with rights for captive use globally) and has started setting up an electrolyser giga-factory, to be commissioned and ramped up in phases over the next few quarters; the business is working towards 3 MMTPA of green hydrogen equivalent capacity by 2032 for global markets, and has entered a 15-year green ammonia offtake agreement with Samsung C&T Corporation with supply commencing in the second half of FY2029. In renewable generation, RIL is developing a 550,000-acre renewable hub in Kutch designed to meet ~10% of India's electricity demand within a decade; at peak installation the site will deploy 55 MWp of solar modules and 150 MWh of battery containers daily, with solar generation expected in FY2026-27 for captive use and green fuel production, supported by a dedicated Kutch-Jamnagar transmission corridor for round-the-clock green power. In Bio Energy, RIL is building India's largest integrated Compressed Biogas (CBG) platform, contributing over 30% of India's CBG production through ~270 retail outlets supplying 40,000+ vehicles daily; CBG production has reached 270+ TPD across 35 operating plants (~700 TPD capacity) and is on track to reach 1,100 TPD with 55 operating plants by end of FY2026-27, alongside commissioning 6 of the largest CBG Complexes (50 TPD+ each) pan-India in FY2026-27; over the next five years RIL targets integrated CBG hubs to achieve 1 million tonnes of annual CBG capacity.

one-line thesis: An "extraordinary" quarter delivered *through* the Strait-of-Hormuz energy shock: O2C EBITDA +17% on ethane-cracking + agile crude sourcing while Asian peers ran 15-20% below capacity, Jio compounded +15% EBITDA (post full 5G capitalisation), and Retail deliberately traded near-term margin to scale digital commerce. The forward narrative is a set of hard targets — Retail EBITDA to 2x in 3 years, RCPL to ₹1 lakh cr by FY30, New Energy to 20 GW solar / 120 GWh battery, and a 168 MW Meta data centre — set against management's refusal to hard-guide capex amid live geopolitical volatility.

- **Petrochem:** polymer demand -22% (price/availability/feedstock); PVC least affected (China coal-PVC), PE most; ethane delta "phenomenally higher."

risks & watch-items:
- **Geopolitics / SOH:** crude availability + valuation swings ("$70 → $85 in days"); management explicitly refused to extrapolate current-month profitability — "everything is based on assumption." Fresh escalation post-ceasefire.
- **O2C realisation gap:** astronomical cracks ≠ profit given premiums/freight/insurance; not steady-state.
- **Retail margin:** short-term % compression while scaling digital; execution on unit economics market-by-market.
- **RCPL:** breakeven EBITDA; profitability contingent on scale/supply-chain build.
- **Jio:** ARPU optics soft QoQ (<1%) due to promotional Homes offers; digital-services margin still below connectivity.
- **JioStar:** real-money-gaming ad ban + US-Iran war hit the ad market.
- **E&P:** KGD6 decline; gas ceiling-price ceiling caps upside.
- LEO/satellite + AI DC capex outlays large and still-evolving.
management quality / tone: Confident, execution-focused, unusually candid about *not* forecasting (CFO Srikanth repeatedly declined capex + next-quarter profitability guidance given live volatility — "a sophisticated way of asking… everything is assumption"). New Energy narrative shifted "from strategy to tangible execution" with on-ground photos. Segment heads gave granular numbers; guidance offered only where conviction is high (Retail 2x, RCPL ₹1 L cr, 20 GW/120 GWh).
non-obvious takeaways:
- The quarter's quality is in *what it absorbed* — SOH closure, LPG 4x diversion, planned turnaround, SAED, under-recoveries — and still grew O2C EBITDA 17%; the ethane edge is the structural why.
- Retail's margin dip is a **choice**, not weakness — absolute EBITDA is the KPI, and online scales faster than stores → revenue growth should accelerate.
- Reliance Intelligence + Meta 168 MW DC quietly reframes Reliance as an AI-infrastructure builder (network+power+managed services end-to-end), leveraging Jamnagar green power.
- Russia losing >40% refining capacity + Middle East capacity loss underpins management's "structurally short refining → strong cracks" thesis.
- Jio's PAT (₹764 cr) optically low purely from expensing (not capitalising) 5G interest — EBITDA is the real signal.

themes.title: Oil & Gas - gas economy (CGD/LNG) + refining/upstream
themes.need: India's gas-economy push now collides with an outright policy reversal. ATGL grew volume 13% to 303 MMSCM and revenue 27% to INR 1,908cr, yet EBITDA FELL sequentially to INR 281cr (~14.7% margin, from INR 310cr) because the government withdrew the pooled-gas mechanism after the West Asia 'peace deal', pushing ATGL to ~15% spot volumes with Brent above $107/bbl; management also noted NWG price is 12% of the Indian crude basket, so a 62% domestic mix protects far less than it looks, and CNG station adds slowed to +5 from +25 in Q4 even as CNG demand grows ~30%. MGL/GUJGASLTD/IGL/IRMENERGY carry the same CGD margin squeeze; PETRONET/OIL/ONGC/IOC ride LNG-infra + domestic-gas; CHENNPETRO/MRPL ride GRM cracks; DEEPINDS/JINDRILL/SEAMECLTD on ONGC E&P capex; AEGISLOG/AEGISVOPAK add LPG/gas terminalling.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- O2C outlook: global oil demand growth expected to be sluggish in FY2026-27 due to higher oil prices and economic slowdown amid the Middle East conflict; refinery and oil-infrastructure damage is likely to take longer to recover, causing continual market volatility.
- O2C outlook: in FY2026-27, volatile product and feedstock prices, supply disruptions from the Middle East, and Government of India directives on SAED, petrochemical feedstock usage and duty exemptions on key petrochemical products may weigh on domestic demand and margins.
- O2C opportunities: India's infrastructure, mobility and industrial growth driving fuel and downstream chemical demand; stable non-OECD oil demand growth and an increasing fuel market deficit; trade deals and GST rationalisation aiding domestic demand growth in polyester and downstream sectors.
- O2C threats: geopolitical tensions, sanctions and tariff pressures causing price and trade volatility; rising Chinese exports and global overcapacity pressuring downstream chemical margins; energy transition, EV growth and carbon regulations reducing long-term fossil-fuel demand.
- Oil and Gas: expanding gas infrastructure is expected to support growth in domestic gas demand, with rising demand from CGD, fertiliser and power sectors; mature-basin natural decline in deepwater assets increases the focus on recovery and capital discipline.
- Digital Services: strong momentum in revenue contribution from non-connectivity digital services (Consumer and Enterprise Cloud Services, managed services for enterprises, integration of Media & Entertainment with connectivity packages, IoT services) alongside core connectivity growth led by 5G adoption and Fixed Wireless Access.
- Retail: growth driven by improved category mix, private label contribution and operating efficiencies across supply chain and fulfilment, with continued strategic brand partnerships (Stella McCartney, Kurt Geiger, Max & Co., Fabletics) reinforcing Reliance Retail as the partner of choice for international brands entering India.
- Oil and Gas: targeted production optimisation initiatives and planned development wells in KG D6 are expected to enhance recovery.
- Oil and Gas: execute targeted infill drilling in R-Cluster and Satellite Cluster, and deploy multilateral horizontal wells (MLW) in the CBM portfolio to enhance productivity and offset mature-basin decline.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Oil and Gas: to maximise recovery from the KG D6 field, four infill wells are planned targeting incremental ~220 BCF of gas, with three additional workover wells planned in FY2026-27 for production sustenance. Exploration surveys (including Controlled Source Electromagnetic Survey) are underway in blocks KG-UDWHP-2018/1, KG-UDWHP-2022/1 and GS-OSHP-2022/1, which have received Petroleum Exploration Licenses under OALP Rounds II, VIII and IX; Infrastructure-led Exploration (ILX) prospects have matured into drilling plans in KG D6. In Coal Bed Methane, a multi-lateral horizontal well (MLW) programme (first of its kind in India) is being implemented in block SP(West)-CBM-2001/1 to reverse field decline — the first campaign is complete and the second is underway; Reliance Gas Pipeline Limited (a subsidiary) operates the 304-km Shahdol-Phulpur pipeline connecting CBM fields to the National Gas Grid. New Energy: the Dhirubhai Ambani Green Energy Giga Complex in Jamnagar is being developed across 5,000 acres with 44 million sq. ft. of manufacturing/operational built-up area, envisioned as the world's most integrated clean-energy manufacturing ecosystem outside China and expected to create over 200,000 green jobs. In Solar PV, core manufacturing assets were commissioned and Phase I became operational in FY2025-26, with cell and module lines being progressively commissioned and HJT cell production ramping up (first 200 MWp of HJT modules delivered); the facility remains on track to scale to 10 GWp per annum with expansion to 20 GWp planned, targeting 26% module efficiency, with polysilicon, glass, ingots and wafers being commissioned in phases toward full integration. The BESS giga-factory is in advanced commissioning, with civil construction complete and equipment installation underway; production will ramp through the second half of 2026, focused on LFP chemistry for utility-scale BESS and mobility, with 40 GWh of annual capacity to be operationalised and a roadmap to 100 GWh. In Green Hydrogen, RIL secured exclusive technology licensing from Nel ASA for alkaline electrolysers in India (with rights for captive use globally) and has started setting up an electrolyser giga-factory, to be commissioned and ramped up in phases over the next few quarters; the business is working towards 3 MMTPA of green hydrogen equivalent capacity by 2032 for global markets, and has entered a 15-year green ammonia offtake agreement with Samsung C&T Corporation with supply commencing in the second half of FY2029. In renewable generation, RIL is developing a 550,000-acre renewable hub in Kutch designed to meet ~10% of India's electricity demand within a decade; at peak installation the site will deploy 55 MWp of solar modules and 150 MWh of battery containers daily, with solar generation expected in FY2026-27 for captive use and green fuel production, supported by a dedicated Kutch-Jamnagar transmission corridor for round-the-clock green power. In Bio Energy, RIL is building India's largest integrated Compressed Biogas (CBG) platform, contributing over 30% of India's CBG production through ~270 retail outlets supplying 40,000+ vehicles daily; CBG production has reached 270+ TPD across 35 operating plants (~700 TPD capacity) and is on track to reach 1,100 TPD with 55 operating plants by end of FY2026-27, alongside commissioning 6 of the largest CBG Complexes (50 TPD+ each) pan-India in FY2026-27; over the next five years RIL targets integrated CBG hubs to achieve 1 million tonnes of annual CBG capacity.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident, execution-focused, unusually candid about *not* forecasting (CFO Srikanth repeatedly declined capex + next-quarter profitability guidance given live volatility — "a sophisticated way of asking… everything is assumption"). New Energy narrative shifted "from strategy to tangible execution" with on-ground photos. Segment heads gave granular numbers; guidance offered only where conviction is high (Retail 2x, RCPL ₹1 L cr, 20 GW/120 GWh).

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Scale and diversification across energy, digital, consumer and media businesses described by the company as 'Sustainable Growth Enablers': technology and consumer-centric platforms, competitive access to capital, strong project management capability, and diversification, integration and cost leadership
- Reliance Retail positioned as India's largest and most profitable omni-channel retailer, with 20,160 stores, 78.3 million sq. ft. retail area and a 387 million registered customer base
- Jio is one of the largest data operators globally (241+ exabytes of traffic in FY2025-26) and the clear market leader in 5G services with 268 million 5G mobility subscribers as of March 2026
- Vertically integrated 'mind-to-shelf' fashion model enabling fresh fashion drops across stores on a roughly 30-day cycle
- Investment-grade credit strength: AAA (Stable) domestic ratings from CRISIL, CARE, ICRA and India Ratings, plus international ratings above India's sovereign (S&P A-, Moody's Baa2), supporting access to capital at competitive cost across currencies/tenors
- Integrated O2C operations providing feedstock flexibility and continuous efficiency improvements, sustaining profitability through operating-rate optimisation amid volatile energy markets

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
- **Geopolitics / SOH:** crude availability + valuation swings ("$70 → $85 in days"); management explicitly refused to extrapolate current-month profitability — "everything is based on assumption." Fresh escalation post-ceasefire.
- **O2C realisation gap:** astronomical cracks ≠ profit given premiums/freight/insurance; not steady-state.
- **Retail margin:** short-term % compression while scaling digital; execution on unit economics market-by-market.
- **RCPL:** breakeven EBITDA; profitability contingent on scale/supply-chain build.
- **Jio:** ARPU optics soft QoQ (<1%) due to promotional Homes offers; digital-services margin still below connectivity.
- **JioStar:** real-money-gaming ad ban + US-Iran war hit the ad market.
- **E&P:** KGD6 decline; gas ceiling-price ceiling caps upside.
- LEO/satellite + AI DC capex outlays large and still-evolving.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- The quarter's quality is in *what it absorbed* — SOH closure, LPG 4x diversion, planned turnaround, SAED, under-recoveries — and still grew O2C EBITDA 17%; the ethane edge is the structural why.
- Retail's margin dip is a **choice**, not weakness — absolute EBITDA is the KPI, and online scales faster than stores → revenue growth should accelerate.
- Reliance Intelligence + Meta 168 MW DC quietly reframes Reliance as an AI-infrastructure builder (network+power+managed services end-to-end), leveraging Jamnagar green power.
- Russia losing >40% refining capacity + Middle East capacity loss underpins management's "structurally short refining → strong cracks" thesis.
- Jio's PAT (₹764 cr) optically low purely from expensing (not capitalising) 5G interest — EBITDA is the real signal.
